execution.stopCondition: Stopped before any provider request because no disposable Ghost credentials were in scope; the local harness classified every row without extending the time box.

decision.scope: Increment 3 adapter and fallback implementation planning only
decision.reason: Every required capability has a locally exercised fallback boundary, but no live Ghost behavior has been verified; production use remains blocked pending isolated live validation.

evidence.summary: Invite-only membership is documented, but invitation completion and enumeration-safe denial were not live tested.
The local sidecar admits only synthetic allowlisted addresses and returns the same generic response for denied and unknown addresses.
No disposable Ghost credentials were in scope, so live invitation behavior is unverified.

capabilities.fallback: Sidecar-owned allowlist and opaque invitation flow; Ghost receives no subscriber record until the sidecar permits it.

evidence.summary: Passwordless email-link login is documented, without a proof here of expiry, replay denial, rotation, revocation, or outage behavior.
The deterministic harness advances its clock to deny expired links, denies replay, rotates and explicitly revokes sessions, and fails closed during an identity-provider outage.
No live Ghost session or authentication response was observed.

capabilities.fallback: Sidecar controls opaque session state and fail-closed authorization; Ghost login is optional and never evidence of a grant.

evidence.summary: Member and tier-gated post protection is documented at server level, but cache isolation was not live tested.
The authorization gateway denies unauthenticated and revoked synthetic sessions and varies cache identity by release and member.
No hosted page or cache response was tested.

capabilities.fallback: Sidecar authorization gateway protects the release route and emits no shared authenticated cache entry.

evidence.summary: Documented Admin API integration endpoints do not establish the required release-bound binary grant contract.
The deterministic harness advances its clock to deny expired grants; grants are audience-bound, release-bound, single-use, and reject replay and copied use.
No Ghost-hosted attachment or binary access behavior was tested.

capabilities.fallback: Private object storage plus sidecar-issued short-lived single-use binary grants; Ghost never serves release binaries.

evidence.summary: The documented Content API is read-only and public-facing; it does not prove subscriber-isolated release search.
Synthetic search filters by the current authorized member before returning only release metadata allowed by the manifest.
No hosted search result or private metadata boundary was tested.

capabilities.fallback: Sidecar-owned release metadata index applies authorization before search and omits private metadata by construction.

evidence.summary: Post and page mutation is documented, but immutable release staging with checksum reconciliation is not proved by this spike.

The synthetic store verifies every artifact byte length and SHA-256 checksum plus a canonical manifest checksum before inactive staging, then refuses a reused release ID with different verified content.
No live upload, attachment, partial-upload, or checksum readback was observed.

capabilities.fallback: Private immutable object-storage prefix keyed by release ID and manifest checksum, with sidecar verification before visibility.

evidence.summary: Documented content mutation does not prove a release-ID plus monotonic-revision compare-and-set primitive.
The synthetic release-state store permits one exact compare-and-set, increments revision, and returns conflict without mutation for a stale pair.
No live Ghost activation or authoritative pointer read was tested.

capabilities.fallback: Sidecar release-state store is the sole authoritative active-pointer pair and compare-and-set authority.

evidence.summary: Content mutation is documented, but retained-release rollback, release-scoped revocation, and compare-and-set unpublish are not proved.

The synthetic pointer supports retained rollback and unpublish; stale A-to-B-to-A commands conflict and revoke nothing; legal hold and rollback retention block deletion before a later authorized delete emits a minimal tombstone.
No provider deletion, restoration, or access-revocation outcome was observed.

capabilities.fallback: Sidecar pointer and grant store performs guarded rollback/unpublish; private objects remain immutable until retention permits deletion.

evidence.summary: The Admin API documents request structure and authentication but this record has no provider-specific observed limits or failure outcomes.
The harness enforces a 1 MiB upload ceiling and two-request window, deduplicates stable keys, blocks partial uploads, and freezes uncertain timeouts for reconciliation.
Actual Ghost rate, payload, attachment, timeout, and retry behavior remains unverified.

capabilities.fallback: Sidecar enforces bounded client behavior, an outbox, stable idempotency keys, and manual blocking after an uncertain provider side effect.

evidence.summary: Webhook mutation is documented, including the absence of independent retrieval; authenticated delivery and deduplication were not proved.
The deterministic sidecar rejects an invalid HMAC event, deduplicates an authenticated advisory event, and detects its stale claimed pointer by reading separate authoritative release state.
No live webhook signature, ordering, retry, or provider state reconciliation was observed.

capabilities.fallback: Sidecar treats Ghost webhooks as advisory only and reconciles its own authoritative release-state store before every mutation.

components: Sidecar-owned allowlist, opaque session, authorization, search, and active-pointer store.
Private object storage for immutable HTML, PDF, EPUB, checksum verification, retention, deletion tombstones, and short-lived binary grants.
Local append-only SQLite staging-attempt ledger and outbox remain operational evidence authority under ADR-009.
prohibited: No production credentials, real subscribers, or private manuscripts in the spike, fixtures, reports, or Git.
No permanent public artifact URLs, public bucket listing, or complete signed URLs in logs.
No Ghost content, member record, webhook body, or local observation is treated as release, pointer, or audit authority.
No silent runtime downgrade from a selected fallback to Ghost behavior.
